the non-partisans' victories are due to the advantage of incumbency, and that the partisan offensive is sluggish.

the non-partisans are more successful in the local elections in the municipalities that are characterized by a higher level of economic development, a higher level of education of voters and a higher level of urbanization.

non-partisans are successful in the municipalities with a small number of inhabitants, in the rural areas, in the regions that are not the centres of the country's political life and in which the local party organizations are not strong. 1 The article concentrates on recent success-es of non-partisans in Polish local govern-ment.

the question of the role of parties in local politics.
the factors determining the variation in the level and structure of party competition in local politics.
the question: why do non-partisans challenge parties in Polish local politics?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Polish case is a unique one and cannot be easily transferred to other countries.
the Polish case is an extreme one.
non-partisans in Poland have been successful in a limited way.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Polish case is an exception in Europe, and that the level of partyness in Polish local government is likely to remain at its current level in the future.
the non-partisans are a heterogeneous group of individuals, whose success in local elections is due to a variety of reasons.
the local government in Poland is not a ‘partisan arena’ but a ‘partisan-free zone’.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the level of partyness in local politics is a result of the balance of power between the local party organisations and the local political elite.

the non-partisan challenge to parties in local politics is not an outcome of a sudden change of the political landscape, nor is it a sign that local politics is becoming increasingly independent of national politics.
